environment.description: Same Spring Boot application deployed on the same EC2 instance, but the origin's security group restricts inbound traffic exclusively to the CloudFront managed prefix list (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing, pl-3b927c52). A CloudFront distribution is configured with a custom origin pointing to the ALB's internal DNS. The distribution uses a Trusted Key Group with an RSA-2048 signing key for generating signed URLs. The CloudFront behavior for /api/v2/* has 'Restrict Viewer Access' set to 'Yes' with the Trusted Key Group, meaning only requests bearing a valid CloudFront signed URL (with Policy, Signature, and Key-Pair-Id query parameters or cookies) are forwarded to origin. Unsigned or tampered requests receive a 403 from CloudFront edge before reaching the origin. The signed URL policy specifies a 30-second TTL and binds to the exact URL path without wildcards in the resource field. The private signing key is stored in AWS Secrets Manager with access restricted to a Lambda function that generates signed URLs only for authenticated users (Cognito JWT validation). Additionally, the CloudFront distribution has a response headers policy that injects 'Content-Security-Policy: default-src self; script-src self' on all responses from the /api/v2/* path pattern.

config.network: Security group inbound restricted to pl-3b927c52 (CloudFront origin-facing IPs only)
config.signing_key_access: Secrets Manager, Lambda-only IAM policy, requires Cognito auth
